correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the exact 12-vertex 30-edge icosahedral graph and ordinary five-cut facet predicate (complements of disconnected induced five-subsets). Enumerated 300 distinct seven-vertex facets and all 2618 faces, dimension-vector 1,12,66,220,495,792,732,300 for dimensions −1..6. Independent direct mod-2 simplicial ranks ∂1..∂6=(11,55,165,330,461,270) corroborate torsion but do not determine integral order. Fresh reimplementation of ordered simplicial Morse matching and signed integral chain cancellation has 1286 matched pairs, critical cells one0, five4, seven5, thirtytwo6 and ∂5 SNF (1,1,1,1,2), ∂6 SNF(1,1), ∂5∂6=0. The image of ∂6 is primitive rank2, equal to the rank2 kernel of ∂5. Thus reduced integral H4=Z/2, H6=Z^30, everything else zero. Pure 6-dimensional shellability would forbid torsion; a wedge of spheres would have torsion-free homology. No higher-graph assertion or integral homotopy classification.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the exact natural icosahedral ordinary five-cut torsion calculation, not a first-ever torsion cut complex. Bayer et al. Remark 4.2 engineered a 16-vertex graph whose 13-cut is an RP2 triangulation; different graph and threshold. Their Theorem 6.1 requires a complete codimension-one skeleton, but the icosahedron has 732 of 924 possible five-faces, so it cannot imply torsion-freeness or the result. The sequel covers disjoint unions, squared paths, grids. An indexed icosahedral ordinary three-cut computes S7∨6 S8 at a different threshold. No exact five-cut SNF/database result was recovered; absence alone not proof of novelty.

The exact finite computation is verified for this one graph; no general Platonic or cut-size theorem is asserted.

value.rationale: A smallest Platonic highly symmetric planar triangulation is a motivated natural graph for cut-complex topology; it exhibits genuine integral 2-torsion in degree 4 of a pure degree-6 complex. This proves nonshellability and rules out any wedge-of-spheres homotopy type, upgrading previously synthetic torsion examples into a complete integral invariant of a natural graph/cut parameter.
